model_annotations.English: The plot illustrates the relationship between block index and sensitivity for 8-bit and 4-bit representations. The x-axis, labeled “Block Index”, has a linear scale ranging from 0 to 31, with tick labels at integer values. The y-axis, labeled “Sensitivity”, has a logarithmic scale ranging from 10⁻⁶ to 10⁻⁴, with tick labels representing powers of ten, and is not regularly spaced. A blue, vertically-striped line represents the 8-bit data, beginning at a sensitivity of approximately 2.1 x 10⁻⁶ at a block index of 0 and increasing to approximately 9.9 x 10⁻⁵ at a block index of 31. A green, vertically-striped line represents the 4-bit data, starting at a sensitivity of approximately 1.5 x 10⁻⁶ at a block index of 0 and increasing to approximately 4.4 x 10⁻⁵ at a block index of 31.
model_annotations.German:
The plot illustrates the relationship between sensitivity and block index for two data sets, represented by different bit widths. The x-axis is labeled “Block Index” and has a linear scale ranging from 0 to 31, with tick labels at integer values. The y-axis is labeled “Sensitivity” and utilizes a logarithmic scale, ranging from 10<sup>-6</sup> to 10<sup>-4</sup>, with tick labels at 10<sup>-6</sup>, 10<sup>-5</sup>, and 10<sup>-4</sup>. 

There is a blue bar series representing “8-Fbit” data; its height increases steadily as the block index increases. Starting at a sensitivity of approximately 2.5 x 10<sup>-6</sup> at block index 0, it rises to a sensitivity of approximately 9.5 x 10<sup>-5</sup> at block index 31. There is also a green bar series representing “4-Fbit” data; its height shows some fluctuation with increasing block index. Beginning with a sensitivity of approximately 2.5 x 10<sup>-6</sup> at block index 0, it features a local minimum with a sensitivity of approximately 1.6 x 10<sup>-6</sup> at block index 7, and then rises to a sensitivity of approximately 6.7 x 10<sup>-5</sup> at block index 31.
